name: Axis Sim Dataset V1
summary: Axis Sim Dataset V1 is over 50,000 human-teleoperated simulation trajectories across 207 manipulation tasks and more than 60,000 scene variants on a simulated Franka Research 3 — pick-and-place, stacking, pouring, tool use and articulated-object manipulation. The interesting part is the accompanying claim, which cuts against the field's habit of filtering hard for near-optimal expert demonstrations: Axis argues quality lives at the distribution level rather than in individual trajectories, and reports continual pretraining lifting LIBERO-Plus success from 83.9% to 88.8%, beating volume-matched baselines and not saturating as data scales. Dataset, training code and benchmarks are public, and it is the most downloaded open Franka simulation corpus on Hugging Face.
innovation: Argues and tests a distribution-level definition of data quality, against the prevailing filter-for-expert-demonstrations practice.
Teleoperated rather than scripted simulation data, which keeps human variability that synthetic generation removes.
matters: If quality really is distributional, the expensive curation pipelines most groups run are optimising the wrong object.
limits: Simulation only, one arm, one gripper — LIBERO-Plus gains need not survive contact with real hardware.
Announced by press release alongside a funding round; no paper, and the scaling claim rests on a single benchmark.
lineage: MimicGen and RoboCasa's synthetic scaling, but collected by teleoperation and argued from distribution coverage.
